definition: Cognitive philology is the science that studies written and oral texts as the product of human mental processes.
details: Studies in cognitive philology compare documentary evidence emerging from textual investigations with results of experimental research, especially in the fields of cognitive and ecological psychology, neurosciences and artificial intelligence. "The point is not the text, but the mind that made it". Cognitive Philology aims to foster communication between literary, textual, philological disciplines on the one hand and researches across the whole range of the cognitive, evolutionary, ecological and human sciences on the other. Cognitive philology: investigates transmission of oral and written text, and categorization processes which lead to classification of knowledge, mostly relying on the information theory; studies how narratives emerge in so called natural conversation and selective process which lead to the rise of literary standards for storytelling, mostly relying on embodied semantics; explores the evolutive and evolutionary role played by rhythm and metre in human ontogenetic and phylogenetic development and the pertinence of the semantic association during processing of cognitive maps; Provides the scientific ground for multimedia critical editions of literary texts. Among the founding thinkers and noteworthy scholars devoted to such investigations are: Alan Richardson: Studies Theory of Mind in early-modern and contemporary literature. Anatole Pierre Fuksas Benoît de Cornulier David Herman: Professor of English at North Carolina State University and an adjunct professor of linguistics at Duke University. He is the author of "Universal Grammar and Narrative Form" and the editor of "Narratologies: New Perspectives on Narrative Analysis". Domenico Fiormonte François Recanati Gilles Fauconnier, a professor in Cognitive science at the University of California, San Diego. He was one of the founders of cognitive linguistics in the 1970s through his work on pragmatic scales and mental spaces. His research explores the areas of conceptual integration and compressions of conceptual mappings in terms of the emergent structure in language. Julián Santano Moreno Luca Nobile Manfred Jahn in Germany Mark Turner Paolo Canettieri

explainer.lead: Cognitive philology treats stories, poems, manuscripts, and conversations as clues to how human minds produce and transmit language. It connects traditional textual scholarship with experiments and ideas from psychology, neuroscience, and artificial intelligence.

tiers.eli5: Imagine finding several versions of the same story and asking not only which words changed, but why a person might have changed them. Cognitive philology compares those clues with what experiments reveal about how people think, communicate, and tell stories. The text is the footprint; the mind that made it is what researchers want to understand.
tiers.practitioner: A practitioner can use cognitive philology as an interdisciplinary study design: analyze textual or oral evidence, then compare it with experimental findings from cognitive or ecological psychology, neuroscience, or artificial intelligence. Depending on the question, the analysis may draw on information theory, embodied semantics, or research on natural conversation. It is not a single software pipeline, and a textual pattern alone should not be treated as evidence for a mental process without suitable experimental comparison.
tiers.paperLevel: Cognitive philology is formally the study of written and oral texts as products of human mental processes, comparing documentary evidence from textual investigation with experimental research. Its topics include textual transmission, knowledge categorization, narrative formation, rhythm and metre in ontogenetic and phylogenetic development, semantic association in cognitive maps, and multimedia critical editions. It is an interdisciplinary research programme rather than a specified algorithm, so it has no single formula or scoring rule.

explainer.example: A researcher collects several oral versions of one story and documents where their episodes and wording differ. They compare this evidence with experimental work on natural conversation and embodied semantics, then examine which selections and changes may contribute to a more conventional literary way of telling the story.

usedIn.name: Textual transmission studies
usedIn.detail: Investigating how oral and written texts change as they are passed on.

usedIn.name: Narrative research
usedIn.detail: Studying how narratives emerge in natural conversation and how storytelling standards develop.

usedIn.name: Knowledge categorization
usedIn.detail: Examining classification processes, often with support from information theory.

usedIn.name: Multimedia critical editions
usedIn.detail: Providing a scientific basis for presenting literary texts and their evidence in multimedia form.

explainer.intuition: A text is both an object to interpret and evidence of the mental activity that created and transmitted it. Cognitive philology puts close textual study and experimental cognitive research into conversation, guided by the idea that the point is not the text itself but the mind that made it.
howItWorks: Select written texts, manuscripts, oral performances, or conversations to investigate.
Use textual and philological methods to identify documentary evidence, variants, and patterns.
Compare those findings with experimental research in relevant cognitive and human sciences.
Interpret processes such as transmission, categorization, narrative formation, or semantic association.
Where appropriate, use the results to support multimedia critical editions.
explainer.whyItMatters: It offers a way to connect evidence preserved in language with explanations of human cognition rather than studying texts and minds in isolation. It also creates common ground between literary and philological disciplines and cognitive, evolutionary, ecological, and human sciences.
misconceptions: It is not concerned only with literary texts; oral texts and natural conversation also fall within its scope.
It does not discard philology, but combines textual investigation with experimental research.
It is not a single AI model or algorithm, but an interdisciplinary field of study.
